name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: One of the highest paid actors in Hollywood history, Arnold Schwarzenegger has earned some $500 million (before taxes and fees) in paychecks and profit-sharing deals from his movies.
He's made even more from early bets on everything from California real estate to stakes in some of the world's most valuable brands.
One of his best bets: Buying a minority stake in fellow billionaire David Booth's Dimensional Fund Advisors when it was managing $12 billion in assets.
Founded in 1996, DFA now has $777 billion of assets under management.
Other valuable investments include a piece of Easton Town Center, the Columbus, Ohio mall created by billionaire Les Wexner, and equity in the Waldorf Astoria hotel in Los Angeles.
Today, Schwarzenegger continues to own several businesses: film and production company Oak Productions, Fitness Publications Inc and film and trademarking holding venture Pumping Iron America.
forbes_facts: Between 1970 and 2019, Schwarzenegger churned out around 50 films that made $5.5 billion at the box office.
Schwarzenegger had a costly divorce in 2021 from Kennedy family member Maria Shriver; he could be worth nearly double his current fortune if the pair had a prenup.

name: Aidyn Rakhimbayev
forbes_bio: Aidyn Rakhimbayev is the co-founder and major shareholder of BI Group, the largest real estate development and construction groups in Kazakhstan.
He founded BI in 1988, growing its opertations to include commercial real estate, education infrastructure, and multi-used urban development projects.
BI Group operates projects in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, the U.S., the UAE, and Azerbaijan.
Rakhimbayev also co-foudned the educational project IQanat, which was the subject of a Harvard Business School case study.
forbes_facts: Rakhimbayev completed triathlons at the 2016 Ironman Barcelona and 2017 Ironman Copenhagen.

name: Alfredo Harp Helu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alfredo Harp Helú's fortune stems from Acciones y Valores de Mexico, also known as Accival, which he cofounded.
In 1991 Accival merged with Mexican bank Banamex to form Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci). Harp Helú then became chairman of the group.
Citigroup acquired Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival for $12 billion in stock and cash in 2001, and Harp Helú joined Citigroup's board.
He has a minority stake in publicly-traded tile producer Internacional de Ceramica.
He owns two Mexican baseball teams, Los Diablos Rojos of Mexico City and Los Guerreros of Oaxaca.
forbes_facts: A baseball enthusiast, he published an autobiography in 2003 titled, "To Live and Die Playing Baseball."
He was kidnapped in 1994 for 106 days and released, reportedly after a payment of $30 million.

name: Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes
forbes_bio: Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes, is an heir to the Brazilian industrial conglomerate Votorantim, which was founded by his grandfather Jose Ermirio de Moraes.
The Votorantim fortune dates back to 1918, when Jose bought a textile factory in Sao Paulo.
Clóvis' mother, Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti, held 25% of the company before giving the stakes to her four children.
The Votorantim group operates in more than 20 countries and has interests in aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, cement and banking.
He has held positions in the group since 1980 and is a director at Hejoassu Administracao, the family's holding company.

name: Yuri Shefler
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Yuri Shefler established the SPI Group, which produced and sold alcohol under 380 brands in 170 countries.
Shefler divided his alcohol business into two companies in 2021: Stoli Group (maker of Stolichnaya vodka) and Amber Beverage Group, which manufactures other spirits.
Amber Beverage Group owns Latvijas balzams, the largest producer of alcoholic beverages in the Baltics, and Amber Production Tequila (KAH Tequila, Rooster Rojo Tequila and Cenote).
He bought Stolichnaya, his best-known brand, from state-owned VVO Soyuzplodoimport for $285,000 in 1997. Russia's Supreme Court deemed the deal illegal in 2021, banning Stoli sales inside Russia.
In 2024, a Russian court declared Shefler an extremist and confiscated his Russian assets for state use.
forbes_facts: Stolichnaya vodka was banned for sale in the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Belgium in 2014.

name: Lloyd Frink
sec_insider_companies: ZILLOW GROUP, INC. (Z AND ZG) - Co -Exec. Chairman & President
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lloyd Frink is the cofounder and executive chair of Zillow Group, an online real estate marketplace.
He and Richard Barton launch Zillow in 2004; it went public seven year later.
Frink previously worked as a senior vice president at Expedia, the travel company founded by Barton.
He also sits on the board of the food delivery firm GrubHub.
forbes_facts: Frink spent a summer interning at Microsoft in 1979, at just 14 years old. He joined the company full-time nine years later.

name: Mimi Haas
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2019-2021); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Mimi Haas, the widow of former Levi Strauss & Co. CEO Peter Haas, owns a 16%  stake in the storied jeans company.
In February 2019, Levi's filed to go public, revealing Mimi as the largest shareholder among several Haas family members.
Mimi Haas served as a board member at Levis Strauss from 2014 to 2018. Peter Haas Jr., Mimi's stepson, is currently a board member.
Altogether six members of the Haas family, which ranks as one of America's richest clans, own a combined 63% of Levi's.
Bavarian immigrant Levi Strauss founded the company in San Francisco in 1853; he invented denim blue jeans in 1873.

name: M.R. Jaishankar
forbes_bio: M.R.Jaishankar is the chairman of South Indian real estate firm Brigade Enterprises, which he founded in 1986.
Brigade has projects in residential, office, retail and hospitality across the southern Indian states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Kerala.
Brigade also runs hotels with 1,500 rooms across five cities, including a Holiday Inn in Chennai.
His daughters Pavitra and Nirupa were appointed as managing director and joint managing director respectively in 2022.
forbes_facts: He started his entrepreneurial career in 1980 with MLR Industries which made chicory for coffee. He shut it down in 1991.
Jaishankar hails from a family of coffee planters from Chikmagalur town in Karnataka state.
